speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) whether the Ministry plans to align measures to manage indiscriminate parking and use of bicycles owned by bike-sharing companies across agencies so that there is a consistent framework that can be implemented in areas managed by HDB, URA and Town Councils; and (b) what are some of the concerns and feedback from the public and operators for some of the measures being considered.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) what is the policy of the Government on regulating dockless bicycle-sharing schemes; (b) since January 2017, what is the number of complaints received on the improper usage of dockless bicycles, including indiscriminate parking and vandalism; and (c) what is the number of dockless bicycles confiscated by the authorities and, of which, how many have been returned to the bicycle sharing firms.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has been coordinating with fellow Government agencies and Town Councils to align the approach against indiscriminate parking of shared bicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, ensure an adequate supply of parking spaces.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA is working with the National Parks Board (NParks), the Housing and Development Board (HDB) and Town Councils to increase bicycle parking capacity within their premises.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These are quicker to implement than bicycle racks and LTA will be providing more, including near bus stops.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Second, ensure the cooperation of the bicycle-sharing companies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA requires them to promptly remove the bicycles which are indiscriminately parked.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is in their interest to cooperate with the authorities.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Any public backlash may make the business model unsustainable.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has received about 70 complaints of indiscriminate parking since the beginning of this year.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This does not include the many comments on forum pages and social media.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At this point in time, there are a total of about 29,000 to 30,000 shared bicycles available in the market.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA is engaging the bike-sharing operators to deploy their fleet in a responsible manner to prevent excessive, indiscriminate parking as well as disamenities to the public.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the Member's last question on geo-fencing, LTA is also working with the various bike-sharing companies to look into some of these innovative and technological solutions so that the prevalence of indiscriminate parking will also be minimised.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One would be the number of lots you have or have planned to put in place, are they sufficient?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I looked at the plan and it is for 2019.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The issues that are faced by my residents and many others in Singapore show that the bikes are indiscriminately parked if there are no parking spaces allocated for them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The regulatory framework today has to take into account that there are not enough parking places and that you need to enforce this a lot more stringently.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second question relates to my Parliamentary Question on the level of enforcement.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: LTA has the enforcement authority but I think most of the other agencies have not implemented this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans to make this more consistent across all agencies?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My Community Club, which is managed by the People's Association, for example, has 65 of these illegally parked.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We have called the operators and they have not collected any of the bikes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They may not be interested in collecting them because the bikes may already have been paid for by deposits.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To a certain sense, there is the business model issue, and there may not be interest for them to also collect the bikes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, the level of enforcement may not be sufficient.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Are there other plans to make enforcement more consistent across all agencies, not just LTA?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Member is right and I agree with his suggestion that we need to have a whole-of-Government approach.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Currently, we have about 130,700 rack and dockless bicycle parking spaces.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will work with Government agencies, including Town Councils, to allow shared bicycles to be parked in all public bicycle parking areas.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are looking into increasing the number of parking places as well.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will also coordinate and strengthen enforcement approaches across these various agencies against indiscriminate bicycle parking.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Last but not least, as part of the whole-of-Government approach, LTA will work with all agencies to harmonise the active mobility infrastructure to make it more convenient and seamless for users.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Are there any more new entrants into the bike-sharing market that have approached LTA recently?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Jurong Town Council has increased the number of yellow boxes for shared bicycles to park but we still face indiscriminate parking.
